Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

Shri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA contends that the police authorities in compliance of the directions issued by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 46998 of 2020 (Junaid Vs State of U.P. and another) reported at 2021 (6) ADJ 511 and with a view to implement the provisions of POCSO Act, 2012 read with POCSO Rules, 2020, have served the bail application upon the victim/legal guardian as well as upon the CWC.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 19.12.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Ram Rawat, learned counsel and Shri Vaibhav Yadav,
learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The incident occurred on 11.11.2014.
2.The applicant was initially enlarged on bail by the learned trial court on 27.11.2014.
3.
The FIR is a fall out over payment of tuition fees to the applicant by the parents of the victim.

4. No allegation of commission of rape by the applicant with the victim was made in the FIR or in the statement of the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
5.
False and aggravated allegations were subsequently made by the victims in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents to save the failing prosecution case.
6. Material inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements of the victims under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
7. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victims has not been produced by the prosecution.
8. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial.
9. The applicant never influenced witnesses or tampered with the evidence.
10. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and shows no signs of an early conclusion.
The applicant cannot be faulted for the delay in the trial.
11. Inordinate delay in the trial will lead to indefinite imprisonment of the applicant without any evidence to implicate him in the offence.
Right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.

There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

sentences.text: In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Vishal Mishra be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties, or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Order Date :- 15.4.2024
